newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse extends gains, profit-taking seen.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse extends gains, profit-taking seen.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse rose for the third consecutive session led by smaller and less liquid stocks but analysts saw speculative demand fading out soon and giving way to profit-taking.
Analysts said, however, any falls should be limited and the market was likely to remain in its longer-term horizontal trend possibly until parliamentary elections.

"Today's heavy supply (at order balancing) isn't signalling a significant (down)trend, but in the next sessions we will have a correction on profit-taking after recent strong gains," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.9 percent, to 16,899.1, and turnover rose 17.6 percent to 219.3 million zlotys on all three markets as 58 issues rose, 25 fell and 12 were flat.

Analysts said Poland's economic growth, falling inflation and expanding capital market were making long-term investors hold on to their shares, despite uncertainty over the outcome of parliamentary polls.

Banks, which fell significantly after weak first quarter results and the central bank's decision last month to raise mandatory reserves on zloty term deposits and foreign currency deposits, were likely to bottom out soon, they said.
They said the largest banks on the exchange, Bank Slaski and BPH, were already looking attractive with valuations of 7.1 and 5.3 times 1997 earnings respectively.
But they said the forthcoming holiday season and general elections scheduled for September were cooling investor mood.
Chipboard maker Grajewo SA started parallel market trade at 142 zlotys, 57.8 percent above the issue price.
Polisa plunged 9.6 percent in thin trade after an eight percent Monday leap and later announcement of a first quarter loss, traders said.
